problem: Whether every Poisson–binomial law with variance V ≥ 1 satisfies a universal variance-scaled lower bound κ/V on the normalized Turán deficit δ_k near the mode, specifically at the first-descent index D, with no dependence on n or the success probabilities.
debate: The literature on log-concavity and ultra-log-concavity of Bernoulli sums, specifically the lower bounds on adjacent-mass ratios of Hillion and Johnson, Johnson, Dümbgen and Wellner, and Pitman, plus the mode-location and maximal-mass results of Darroch and of Bobkov, Marsiglietti and Melbourne.
gap: The existing lower bounds on δ_k depend on n, on the p_i, or on k rather than on V, and all of them degenerate near the mode when summands with p_i near 0 and near 1 pile up at fixed variance; the mode and maximal-mass results give no bound on δ_k at all.
contribution: A proof that V δ_D ≥ 1/4, a binomial family showing the best constant is at most 1/3, consequences δ_k ≥ 1/(4V+|k−D|) everywhere on the support and 1/(4V+1) ≤ δ_c < 2/V at the rightmost mode, and an application to half-circle eigenvalue counts of Haar unitary matrices that improves order 1/N to order 1/log N.
note: The problem, gap and result are stated cleanly, but the opening never says what a variance-scaled bound on δ_D is good for beyond its own sake, and with the constant pinned only between 1/4 and 1/3 and the proof resting on a computer-assisted step, a referee will ask why this is not just a curiosity unless you put a concrete downstream use on page 1.
